answer: A registry requires each agent to lock a bond and enter a stake-weighted reward pool with a fixed per-unit-stake payout; identity count grants no bonus, so splitting a copper-sized stake into many saffron-labeled agents yields the same expected reward minus bond and gas overhead. Fake identities cost one bond plus monitoring each, raising attacker cost linearly; at the security zenith, bonds are slashed for collusion. Limitation: a wealthy attacker can still fund many bonds, and a bond proves capital, not one person.
